long_biography.plain_text:
Rafic Hariri entered Saudi Arabia's construction boom after working as a teacher and accountant. A demanding hotel project in Taif brought royal recognition, and he acquired the French contractor Oger to create Saudi Oger. The group expanded across construction and other sectors, turning its founder into one of the Middle East's most prominent businessmen.

In Lebanon, Hariri financed education and relief programmes before becoming a Saudi intermediary during the civil war. He helped prepare the 1989 Taif Agreement and later led five governments across two terms as prime minister. His reconstruction programme modernised Beirut but also became associated with rising public debt and conflicts between his commercial and political roles. His assassination in central Beirut in 2005 reshaped Lebanese politics and prompted an international investigation.
